newsitem.title: INDIA: Four injured in grenade attack in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Four injured in grenade attack in Kashmir.

text.p: Four people were wounded when suspected separatist militants hurled a grenade at the Congress party's headquarters in the troubled Jammu and Kashmir state on Monday, Indian police said.
The grenade exploded outside the heavily-guarded building in the heart of Srinagar, the state's summer capital, injuring three paramilitary troopers and a party activist, they said.
Congress is one of the parties contesting the first local assembly elections in the state since 1987. The first three phases of voting have been held, and the last is set for September 30.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence during nearly seven years of militancy in the state.
Dozens of separatist groups which oppose Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir have opposed the elections, which are aimed at paving the way to an end to direct federal rule over the state.
The Congress party headquarters in Srinagar is surrounded by dozens of paramilitary troopers.

Some 20 political workers have been killed in violence during the month-long campign. More than a dozen candidates, including Farooq Abdullah, the leader of Kashmir's biggest party, the National Conference, have survived attempts on their lives.
The counting of ballots in the assembly elections will start on October 1. Results are expected several days later.
